tldr: Headlines globally frame Serbia's snap election as a political power move by Vucic to extend his rule through the prime-ministerial seat, with roughly a third of titles contextualising the dissolution within the protest movement — but the Novi Sad corruption backdrop, judicial failures, and EXPO 2027 rationale central to body coverage are invisible at headline level.

frames.sub_frame: Vucic snaps election to extend hold on power

evidence.quote: Serbia's Vucic Calls Early Parliamentary Elections
dissolves parliament as snap elections called
more than a year ahead of schedule
after nearly two years of protests
Šta kažu studenti, a šta stranke i analitičari

single_outlet_findings.finding: Only headline explicitly framing the election as a test of Vucic's 'hold on power' — peer wire services (Reuters, AFP) report procedurally (dissolution/call), while AP foregrounds the power-contest angle at title level.

Only headline predicting electoral fraud ('najbrutalniju krađu' — 'most brutal theft'), the sole adversarial framing of the election process rather than the political outcome — a local Balkans angle entirely absent from international coverage.

Only headline emphasising the schedule disruption ('more than a year ahead of schedule'), framing the election as an institutional abnormality rather than a political or protest-driven event — a procedural-irregularity angle visible only in the exiled Russian outlet.

bottom_line: The headline layer universally advertises a Vucic power-retention manoeuvre, with a minority of outlets surfacing the protest movement as context; the corruption backdrop, EXPO 2027 justification, and student-list challenger that drive body coverage are entirely absent at the title layer.
